text: They soon crossed the outposts, passed through the empty town of Colombes, and found themselves among small vineyards that sloped down to the Seine. <break time="0.8s" /> It was about eleven oclock, and on the other side of the river, the village of Argenteuil seemed dead. <break time="0.8s" /> Above it rose the heights of Orgemont and Sannois, and the great plain toward Nanterre lay empty, with only its bare cherry trees. <break time="0.8s" /> Pointing at the hilltops, Sauvage said, The Prussians are up there, and a strange fear froze the two friends. <break time="0.8s" /> They had never seen a Prussian, yet for months they had felt them all around Paris, unseen but all powerful, ruining France and starving the city. <break time="0.8s" /> What if we met some of them, Morissot asked, and Sauvage answered with a Parisian joke, We would offer them some fried fish. <break time="0.8s" /> Still they hesitated, but at last they crept down through the vines, bent low, their eyes anxious and their ears listening. <break time="0.8s" /> After running across a strip of bare ground, they hid among the dry reeds, and Morissot put his ear to the ground, hearing nothing. <break time="0.8s" /> Sure that they were alone, they began to fish, and soon the little silver gudgeons were biting one after another, filling them with delight.
